title: Pineapple Tallow Balm: The Weird Jar That Made My Skin Happy
body:
Okay so I opened this jar. It was Tuesday night, I think. My hands were wrecked from washing them like a hundred times that day. Dry. Cracked. The kind of dry where lotion just sits on top and does nothing. I had this little jar of whipped tallow balm on my counter for a week. The pineapple one. I kept looking at it. Beef fat. For your face. And hands. And whatever. It sounded insane. But my skin was so mad at me, I was like, fine. Let’s try the weird beef jar.

The first thing was the smell. I was braced for, I don’t know, cooked meat? Grease? Something gross. But it wasn’t. It smelled like… pineapple. But not fake. Not like a cleaner. More like if you walked past one of those fruit stands in the summer. Sweet. Bright. It didn’t smell like skincare. It smelled like a vacation I couldn’t afford. I just sat there for a second sniffing it. My cat looked at me like I was an idiot. Anyway, that pineapple tallow balm smell was the first surprise.

I scooped a little. The texture was… different. Not like any cream I’ve used. Thick but light? It’s whipped beef tallow, they said. From grass-fed cows in France. It felt cool on my fingers. Then I rubbed it on the back of my hand. It melted. Like, actually vanished. My skin just drank it. No greasy film. No shiny residue. It was just gone, and my skin felt… quiet. Not screaming at me anymore. I remember thinking, huh. That’s new.

## How I Ended Up Putting Beef Fat on My Face

Look, I’ve tried everything. The expensive stuff in the fancy glass bottles. The drugstore stuff. My bathroom cabinet is a graveyard of half-used things that promised miracles and delivered disappointment. My skin is sensitive. It gets red. It gets dry patches. It’s a whole drama. I saw people talking about beef tallow skincare online and I scrolled past it for months. It sounded like a joke. Or a weird homesteader thing.

But then it was spring, and the weather couldn’t decide what to do. One day hot, next day windy. My skin was freaking out. Flaky here, oily there. A mess. I was on Etsy looking for a gift and this shop popped up. All these tallow balms. The pictures were simple. The reviews were… intense. People were obsessed. I figured, what’s the worst that could happen? I’d be out like thirty bucks. So I got the pineapple scented tallow balm. Because if I was gonna smear animal fat on myself, it might as well smell like a piña colada.

It sat on my dresser. I’d see it and go, “Later.” But that Tuesday, I just went for it. After the hand test, I was curious. I washed my face. Put a tiny bit of this natural pineapple skincare stuff on my cheeks. Braced for a breakout. For clogged pores. For something to go wrong.

Nothing went wrong.

## What This Stuff Actually Does (To My Skin, Anyway)

So the science, from what I read while avoiding work, is that beef tallow is weirdly close to the oils our own skin makes. Our sebum. So it recognizes it. It doesn’t just sit there—it gets absorbed. Deep. This particular balm is whipped, so it’s this airy, almost fluffy texture that melts on contact. It’s not greasy. That’s the wild part.

I started using it at night. After I brush my teeth, before I get into bed. The routine became: wash face, stare at phone for too long, remember the jar, put some on. The pineapple scent is the best part. It’s cheerful. It doesn’t smell like medicine or a spa. It smells like a fruit. It makes the whole thing feel less serious. Less like a chore. I’d put it on and my room would smell like summer for a minute. My boyfriend asked if I was eating candy in bed.

Within a few days, the dry patches on my forehead were just… gone. Not covered. Gone. My skin felt even. Not tight after washing. The little fine lines around my eyes—I’m in my thirties, they’re there—looked less… thirsty. They weren’t erased. Nothing erases them. But they looked softer. Like my skin was actually hydrated, not just pretending to be.

I started using it on my elbows. My knees. Anywhere that felt like sandpaper. Same thing. It just worked. I didn’t expect much but honestly, this tallow balm works. It’s boringly effective. It’s not magic. It’s just giving your skin what it actually needs, I guess.

## My Skin Now (And A Weird Tangent)

It’s been a few weeks. Maybe a month? I don’t keep track. I’m on my second jar now. I got one for my mom, too. She called me and was like, “What is this pineapple-smelling beef stuff?” and I was like, “Just try it.” Now she uses it.

My skin is calm. That’s the best word. It’s not “glowing” or “radiant” or any of those words they use in ads. It’s just calm. It doesn’t hurt. It doesn’t itch. It feels like skin, not a problem I have to solve. I used to have this expensive cream that came in a silver jar. It cost more than my electric bill. It did nothing. This jar from an Etsy shop costs less than a dinner out and it… works. It’s weird.

Oh, a tangent. The other day I was putting it on and I remembered this hotel soap from a trip to Florida like ten years ago. It was shaped like a seashell and smelled like fake coconut. This smells nothing like that. But it triggered the memory. Weird how smells do that. This smells better. Realer. Anyway.

I use it in the morning sometimes too, if I’m feeling dry. A tiny bit. It sinks in so fast I can put sunscreen over it right away. No pilling. No weird layers. It just… becomes my skin.

## Would I Buy This Pineapple Tallow Balm Again?

Yeah. I already did.

It’s not a cult thing. I’m not a tallow evangelist. But I found something that fixes my dry, angry skin without making it greasy or causing more problems. And it smells like pineapple. It makes me smile when I open the jar. In the middle of a stressful week, that two-second hit of tropical fruit smell is a nice little break. A mini vacation in a jar.

It’s simple. It’s one ingredient, basically, plus some essential oil for scent. No crazy chemical list I can’t pronounce. I know what’s in it. Beef fat and pineapple. That’s it. In a world of a million products with a million promises, that’s kind of refreshing.

So if your skin is being difficult, if you’ve tried the lotions and the potions and you’re still dealing with dry patches or that tight feeling… maybe try the weird beef jar. The pineapple tallow balm one. It might just work.

## Quick Questions I Get Asked

**Is beef tallow good for your face?**
Yeah, surprisingly. From what I get, it’s really similar to the oils our skin makes naturally. So it absorbs deep instead of sitting on top. It’s like giving your skin back what it already knows how to use. My sensitive face loves it.

**Does tallow balm clog pores?**
I was worried about this. But no, not for me. Because it absorbs so completely, it doesn’t just clog stuff up. It’s non-comedogenic, which is a fancy way of saying it shouldn’t block pores. My skin actually cleared up a bit.

**What does pineapple tallow balm smell like?**
Like actual pineapple. Sweet and fruity, but not in a candy or fake way. It’s bright and cheerful. It smells like summer. It’s the best part, honestly. Makes using it feel fun, not clinical.

Anyway. That’s my take. My skin’s happy, I’m happy. I’m probably gonna order another one soon.
